Ground mismatch: LAC are run-first (40% pass when leading) into a BUF front that bleeds 126 rush yds/game and 0.49 RB1 rushing scores. Omarion Hampton is a centerpiece.

The BUF host the LAC as favorites of 2.5, with the total set at 48.5 — a market that implies a BUF 26–23 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 26% of its snaps with BUF in front, 39% within one score, and 34% with BUF chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 2.5 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

Ladd McConkey draws a plus matchup — BUF concede 64 yds/game to WR1s (league ~58), and LAC funnel 23% of targets his way. A rec-yards spot.

BUF — a run-heavy offense

BUF are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 39% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

James Cook (14 carries, 69 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Khalil Shakir projects for 6 targets and 53 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Dalton Kincaid (TE, 4 targets, 29 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

LAC — a run-heavy offense

LAC are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 40% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Omarion Hampton (10 carries, 42 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Ladd McConkey projects for 5 targets and 44 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Oronde Gadsden II (TE, 3 targets, 30 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 2-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
